TsBST and ROY.MARKET a Moscow non-profit, its military marketplace, and the drone-war supply around it

An open-source investigation of ANO «TsBST», a Moscow non-profit for the drone industry, and of the companies, products, sales and handovers to military units that connect to it. Every claim rests on an archived document and is graded by how well that document shows it.

Translation“TsBST together with United Russia and the Nasha Pravda foundation delivered thousands of items to the front for destroying the enemy. […] Together with the party and PSB we launched the military marketplace «Roymarket». The platform has been tested.”RussianЦБСТ вместе с Единой Россией и фондом «Наша правда» поставили на фронт тысячи изделий для уничтожения врага. […] Вместе с партией и ПСБ запустили военный маркетплейс «Роймаркет». Платформа протестирована.Aleksandr SidyakinRussianАлександр Геннадьевич Сидякин, secretary of TsBST's supervisory board and head of United Russia's central executive committee, on TsBST's year, Telegram, 15.12.20251

How we got here

We did not set out to investigate TsBST. We were following military goods on a consumer marketplace, and a new marketplace came looking for the same sellers.

  1. We had been watching Wildberries

    The investigation started as WB Watch, a tracker of military goods sold on Russia's largest consumer marketplace. It found a large, open trade in kit for the war.

    7,666military-item listings
    89%shipped from Wildberries' own warehouses
    802sellers

  2. Then a military marketplace announced itself

    In December 2025 Sidyakin wrote that the party, Bank PSB and TsBST had launched a military marketplace. In August 2026 the platform opened to outside sellers and named the ones it wanted first.

    Translation“The online marketplace ROY.MARKET has opened a protected sales channel for manufacturers, distributors and professional sellers of dual-use goods. First of all it invites legal entities already working on Wildberries, Ozon and other universal marketplaces.”RussianОнлайн-маркетплейс РОЙ.МАРКЕТ открыл защищённый канал продаж для производителей, дистрибьюторов и профессиональных селлеров товаров двойного назначения. В первую очередь площадка приглашает к сотрудничеству юрлица, которые уже работают на Wildberries, Ozon и других универсальных маркетплейсах.ROY.MARKET's announcement, 13.08.20262

    Its target was the seller base we had already mapped.

  3. The site hid its operator. An older copy did not

    The platform's public terms print the operator as “OOO «****»”. A copy archived on 22.08.2026 names it: OOO «MPTM»RussianООО «МПТМ», INN 9714068459. TsBST's own report to the Justice Ministry lists the same company as one it has taken part in since the day it was registered.

    Lines as printed in each document, rendered in English; the Russian original is under RU. The masked version shows the requisites only after login.

  4. First guess: the usual sellers, plus TsBST's residents

    If the platform recruits Wildberries sellers, and TsBST runs a residency for drone makers, the likely suppliers are makers that are both. We checked every maker on file against the Wildberries sellers by INN.

  5. The check missed the best case

    «Bulat», a drone detector shown at Dronnitsa 2025, a showcase TsBST takes part in, returned nothing: no Wildberries seller carries its maker's INN. The detector is on sale all the same, through dealers and sole traders. A sanctions screen keyed on the maker's identifier would make the same mistake.

  6. The marketplace is one outlet among several

    Asked whether the new «Bulat» would go on ROY.MARKET, 3mx answered:

    Translation“All our products can be bought only from us on the site 3mx.ru or from our dealers.”RussianВсю нашу продукцию можно приобрести только у нас на сайте 3mx.ru или у наших дилеров.3mx, in its customer chat, 02.09.202612

    The detector reaches units another way: a foundation that co-founded TsBST buys it and posts the handovers. So we stopped following the platform and started following products, from the maker to the people who receive them.

The network on file

The investigation's registry links 70 organisations to TsBST: 60 through a document (a register entry, a contract, TsBST's own posts), 10 on their own word or press reports alone. 25 of them are on at least one sanctions list. Counted from the registry on 23.10.2026.

How to read the evidence

  • Documented A primary document shows it: a register extract, a state contract, an annual filing, a trademark or patent record.
  • Reported One party's own word (its posts, its website, its listings), or the press. Donors' handover posts are graded here until a second source confirms them.
  • Not documented Drawn to complete the picture, but no document on file shows it. The line's own note says what is missing.

Red marks only a sanctions listing, and always names the regimes. Names appear as registered, in Russian; a company known by its brand is shown by the brand, with the registered name beneath it.

How this is made

  • Facts come from the original Russian documents, read in full: company register extracts, annual accounts, procurement records, trademark records, court filings and the parties' own Telegram posts and websites. Summaries and machine translations are leads, never sources.
  • Every document is archived and hashed when it is collected. Each note at the end of a page says what the document is and links to it where a public copy exists.
  • Pictures are evidence only for what they show, and each says who published it. Faces of people taking part are shown; nobody is named from a face.

What this does not show

  • A handover to a unit does not show that the equipment was used in combat. Some recipients are rear units.
  • TsBST's share in the company that runs ROY.MARKET is not stated in any document on file, and since 15.07.2026 the company register withholds who owns that company15.
  • A US sanctions entry under a similar name belongs to a different company registered in Tula. TsBST itself is not shown here as sanctioned by the US.
  • This is a draft. The earlier case studies and company profiles were withdrawn while the site is rebuilt around chain views.
